Marked as false positive in coverity.

This check is required and works as expected on `native_posix_64`.

review_comments: Question: If you compile the code for native_posix AMD64, wouldn't that make `off_t` `long long`, aka `int64_t`?

```
int main(void)
{
        printf("Hello World! %s\n", CONFIG_BOARD);
        printf("%u\n", sizeof(off_t));
        return 0;
}
```

```
$ ./build/zephyr/zephyr.elf 
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v3.5.0-2011-g716de6fef2c6 ***
Hello World! native_posix
4
```

```
$ lscpu | head -n1
Architecture:                    x86_64
```
Which is curious because it is `int64_t` outside of Zephyr.

Same change

```
west build -b native_posix_64 -d delete-me samples/hello_world/
...
$$ delete-me/zephyr/zephyr.elf
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v3.4.0-7401-g716de6fef2c6 ***
Hello World! native_posix_64
8
```

> Which is curious because it is `int64_t` outside of Zephyr.

Probably Zephyr env does not set _FILE_OFFSET_BITS for for sdk?

ack, I wasn't aware there is a separate native_posix_64 board.

I assume the next step would be to mark this bug as false-positive?
